ingredients.raw: ½ cup extra virgin olive oil
1 3- to 4-pound weakfish, bluefish or sea bass, filleted, or 2 fillets, each about 1 to 1 ½ pounds
ingredients.preparation: bluefish or sea bass, filleted, or 2 fillets, each about 1 to 1 ½ pounds

ingredients.raw: Salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.item: salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.raw: 2 big bunches basil, about 1 pound total

steps.text: Heat grill, preferably with hardwood charcoal fuel. Brush grates with a tablespoon of olive oil.
Place fillets on a platter, brush each on both sides with 1 ½ tablespoons olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Remove ¼ cup basil leaves from bunches and chop very fine. Mince garlic. Mix chopped basil and garlic with remaining oil, season with salt and pepper and set aside.

When grill is hot, place grates about four inches above heat. Pile remaining basil across grates, covering just enough area to hold fish. Place fillets, skin side up, on bed of basil. Allow to cook until most of basil is shriveled and burned, 5 to 7 minutes, and fillets are cooked at least halfway through at thickest point. Use one or two large spatulas to flip fish fillets off basil, onto their skin side and directly on grill. Scrape most of burned basil out of the way. Continue grilling until fish is just cooked through and skin is crisp, 8 to 10 minutes longer.
Lift fillets off grill and transfer them, skin side down, to a serving platter. Remove any burned bits of basil. Add vinegar to basil and oil mixture and drizzle over fish, then serve.

ingredients.raw: 2 cups milk, or half and half
Salt, white pepper and lemon juice, as desired
ingredients.preparation: white pepper and lemon juice, as desired

steps.text: Trim cauliflower and place in large pot. Add lemon juice and water to cover. Cover pot, bring to boil and simmer until just tender (test with skewer). Remove from heat and let stand in water until needed.
Cook onions in water to cover until tender. Drain (reserving water) and puree onions in blender with mustard and horseradish. Reserve.

Melt butter in saucepan, taking care not to burn. Add flour, whisking vigorously. Add milk slowly, whisking to make sure it is fully incorporated, to form white sauce. Stir in onion puree and season to taste with salt, pepper and lemon juice. Thin sauce as desired by adding reserved onion water.
Simmer bockwurst, uncovered, over very low heat 5 minutes. Drain, cool slightly and peel off casings. Cut each wurst into thirds crosswise.
Drain cauliflower, slice into large, thin pieces and place in deep, ovenproof dish. Add bockwurst and pour on sauce. Cover and heat through in slow (200 degree) oven.

name: Wedge Salad With Buttermilk-Blue Cheese Dressing
author: Amanda Hesser

ingredients.raw: ¼ pound smoked slab bacon, cut into ¼-inch cubes
6 slices white bread, crusts removed and cut in half
ingredients.preparation: crusts removed and cut in half

ingredients.raw: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.item: kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.raw: 1 ½ heads iceberg lettuce, trimmed and cut through the core into 12 wedges
ingredients.preparation: trimmed and cut through the core into 12 wedges

ingredients.raw: 3 scallions, green part only, cut in thin slices on a sharp bias
ingredients.preparation: green part only, cut in thin slices on a sharp bias

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees. In a medium skillet over medium heat, cook bacon until crisp. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels, reserving the skillet with bacon fat. Brush bread slices on both sides with bacon fat. Place bread on a baking sheet, and bake until golden brown, turning once, about 5 minutes a side. Remove from oven, and reserve.
In a small bowl, combine buttermilk, cheese, lemon juice, vinegar, shallots, parsley and cayenne. Whisk to blend. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
On each of 6 plates, place 2 slices of bread. Arrange a lettuce wedge on top of each bread slice.
Pour dressing over the wedges. Sprinkle with bacon and scallions. Serve.

ingredients.raw: 1 ¼ pounds spinach in bulk or 1 ½ 10-ounce packages of spinach
ingredients.item: spinach in bulk or 1 ½ 10-ounce packages of spinach

steps.text: Pick over the spinach to remove and discard any tough stems or blemished leaves. Rinse well and drain.
Bring water to the boil and add the spinach. Let cook 2 minutes and drain, pressing or squeezing to extract as much liquid as possible from the leaves.

Heat 1 tablespoon of the butter in a saucepan and add the flour, stirring with a wire whisk. When blended add the milk, stirring vigorously with the whisk. Cook, stirring, until the mixture is thickened and smooth. Add salt, pepper, nutmeg and cayenne pepper.
Put the spinach into the container of a food processor and blend thoroughly, stirring down as necessary. There should be about 1 cup.
Put the spinach in the sauce and stir to blend. Bring to the simmer and swirl in the remaining tablespoon butter.

raw.total: About 2 hours 30 minutes, plus 2 hours' refrigeration

ingredients.raw: ⅓ cup finely chopped dried apricots
Unsalted butter to grease a 5-cup ring mold
ingredients.item: unsalted butter to grease a 5-cup ring mold

ingredients.raw: Zest of 2 navel oranges, cut into thin strips, for garnish
ingredients.preparation: cut into thin strips, for garnish

ingredients.raw: 2 navel oranges, peeled, thinly sliced and cut in half, for garnish
ingredients.preparation: peeled, thinly sliced and cut in half, for garnish

steps.text: Combine the rice and water in a small saucepan and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat, cover and simmer for 30 minutes, or until all the water has evaporated. Uncover and set aside.
Meanwhile, combine the currants and apricots with the rum in a small bowl.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees. Butter a five-cup ring mold. Bring at least three cups of water to a boil.

Scald the milk and cream in a saucepan. Combine the sugar and egg yolks in a large bowl and beat until light in color. Add the scalded milk and cream to the yolks in a slow steady stream, beating constantly with a wire whisk. Stir in the salt, orange extract and coriander. Add the rice and currant-apricot mixture.

Ladle the mixture into the buttered mold, distributing the rice evenly. Place the filled mold in a large pan and pour enough boiling water around the mold to come halfway up its sides. Carefully transfer to the lower third of the preheated oven and bake for 60 to 70 minutes, or until a knife inserted into the center of the pudding comes out clean. The edges will pull away slightly from the mold and the top will be browned.

Remove from the oven and let the mold stand for about 20 minutes in the water. Run a sharp knife around the outside and inside edges, shaking to be sure the pudding is completely loosened. Wipe off any water. Place a large plate over the mold and carefully invert. Remove the mold, cover lightly with foil and refrigerate for one to two hours, or until cool but not cold.
To serve, sprinkle the orange zest over the pudding and layer the orange slices evenly around the outside.

ingredients.raw: Freshly ground black pepper to taste
ingredients.item: freshly ground black pepper to taste

ingredients.raw: 2 ounces Cheddar cheese, preferably New York State sharp, thinly sliced
ingredients.preparation: preferably New York State sharp, thinly sliced

steps.text: Preheat the broiler.
Remove the crusts of the bread. Cut the slices diagonally in half to make 4 triangles. Lightly toast the bread.

In a bowl, combine the butter, Worcestershire sauce, pepper and mustard. Spread the mixture onto the toast. Top with the Cheddar cheese. Place under the broiler and heat until bubbly, about 2 to 3 minutes. Serve at once.

name: Welsh Rarebit
author: Mark Bittman
description: Anyone can lay a few slices of cheese on toast and melt them, but creating a thick sauce of cheese, beer and spices and then spreading it on toast creates one of the best late-night snacks I know. This is Welsh rarebit, or rabbit, a traditional British dish whose name has a long and complicated history, one we will not go into here.

ingredients.raw: 1 tablespoon mustard powder, or to taste
½ teaspoon cayenne, or to taste
¾ cup strong dark beer, like Guinness
2 tablespoons Worcestershire sauce, or to taste
1 pound Cheddar, Double Gloucester or other English cheese (or other good semi-hard cheese, like Comté or Gruyère, or a mixture), grated
ingredients.preparation: Double Gloucester or other English cheese (or other good semi-hard cheese, like Comté or Gruyère, or a mixture), grated

steps.text: Put butter in a saucepan over medium heat and, as it melts, stir in flour. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until golden brown and very fragrant, 3 to 5 minutes. Stir in mustard and cayenne, then whisk in beer and Worcestershire sauce.
When mixture is uniform, turn heat to low and stir in cheese, again stirring until smooth. Remove from heat and pour into a broad container to set (you can refrigerate for up to a day at this point).
Spread mixture thickly on toast and put under broiler until bubbly and edges of toast are crisp. Serve immediately.

ingredients.raw: 8 ounces (2 sticks) unsalted butter, at room temperature

steps.text: Place the butter in a large bowl and cream at high speed until fluffy. Add the sugars and beat until light and fluffy, about 4 minutes, scraping down sides of bowl occasionally. Beat in eggs, one at a time, until completely mixed.

In a separate bowl, mix flour, salt and baking soda. Add to the butter mixture at low speed until just combined and add vanilla extract. Beat on medium speed, scraping bowl down, until blended. Do not overmix.
Add chocolate chunks and mix till thoroughly combined. Refrigerate batter until cold, preferably overnight.

Preheat a conventional oven to 350 degrees or a convection oven to 300 degrees, and line several baking sheets with parchment paper. Drop heaping spoonfuls of batter 2 inches apart on the lined baking sheets and bake, turning tray once, until golden brown around edges and soft (but not bubbly), about 9 minutes in a convection oven or 12 in a conventional one. Cool on a wire rack.

ingredients.raw: 3 tablespoons curry powder, preferably West Indian style
1 medium onion, peeled and cut in ¼-inch dice
ingredients.preparation: peeled and cut in ¼-inch dice

ingredients.raw: 4 medium cloves garlic, smashed, peeled and minced
1 pound mashing potatoes, cooked, peeled, cooled and cut into ½ inch cubes
ingredients.preparation: cooked, peeled, cooled and cut into ½ inch cubes

ingredients.raw: 2 medium ribs celery, peeled and cut in ¼-inch dice
ingredients.preparation: peeled and cut in ¼-inch dice

ingredients.raw: 1 medium red pepper, seeded and cut in ¼-inch dice
ingredients.preparation: seeded and cut in ¼-inch dice

ingredients.raw: 1 medium jalapeno pepper, seeded and minced
2 cups flaked leftover cooked fish such as salmon, cod or red snapper
ingredients.item: flaked leftover cooked fish such as salmon

steps.text: Heat a large nonstick pan over medium heat. Add mustard seeds and cook, shaking pan, for 40 seconds, until seeds start to pop. Add butter and let it melt. Lower heat to medium-low. Stir in the curry powder and cumin. Cook, stirring, for 40 seconds.
Stir in the onion and cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic, ginger and anise seed. Cook, stirring, for 5 minutes.

Add potatoes, raise heat to medium and cook, turning occasionally, for 9 minutes or until potatoes begin to brown. Stir in the celery, red pepper and jalapeno pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 minutes.

Meanwhile whisk together the egg, milk, salt and mint. Pour this over the potato mixture. Stir in the fish and lime juice. Press the mixture into the pan with the back of a spoon to make a cake. Cook, over medium heat, for 15 minutes, until the cake is set and the bottom has formed a crust.
Invert onto a large round serving platter so the crusty side is up.

ingredients.raw: ¼ pound corned beef in one piece
½ Scotch bonnet pepper or other small hot chili, seeded and minced, or hot red pepper flakes or cayenne pepper to taste
ingredients.item: scotch bonnet pepper or other small hot chili
ingredients.preparation: seeded and minced, or hot red pepper flakes or cayenne pepper to taste

ingredients.raw: 2 cups shredded callaloo, spinach, mustard greens or other greens
ingredients.preparation: spinach, mustard greens or other greens

ingredients.raw: ½ pound yuca, peeled and diced
¾ cup diced chayote or yellow squash

steps.text: Dice the sausage, place it in a 3- to 4-quart saucepan and cook over medium heat until lightly browned. Dice the corned beef, add it and continue to cook a few minutes. Add the onion, scallions, bay leaf and thyme, and continue to cook until the onion is tender. Stir in the hot chili or pepper.
In a mortar or spice grinder, crush the allspice and peppercorns and add them to the pot. Stir, then add the stock. Bring to a simmer, and add the greens. Cook for 20 minutes.
Add the carrot, yuca and squash and cook about 10 minutes longer. Taste, adjust the amount of pepper if necessary and season with salt. Remove the bay leaf and thyme before serving.

name: West Lake Beef Soup
author: Cybelle Tondu
description: This velvety, quick-cooking  Chinese soup is a comforting classic named after a scenic lake near the southern city of Hongzhou, where the dish may have originated. The key to its refined character lies in the careful layering of textures: pillowy ground beef, gossamer egg ribbons and silky tofu, all suspended in a thickened, ginger-perfumed broth. Plenty of shiitake mushrooms add earthy depth, while fresh cilantro brightens each spoonful. Pour the egg whites from high above the pot for the thinnest stream and substitute scallions or watercress if serving to the cilantro-averse.

ingredients.raw: 1 (2-inch) piece fresh ginger, halved and lightly crushed
1 tablespoon Shaoxing wine or dry sherry
1 cup finely chopped shiitake mushrooms (from 3 to 4 large shiitakes)
ingredients.item: finely chopped shiitake mushrooms (from 3 to 4 large shiitakes)

ingredients.raw: 1 cup finely chopped cilantro leaves and tender stems, plus more for serving
ingredients.item: finely chopped cilantro leaves and tender stems

steps.text: In a medium pot, combine the broth and ginger and bring to a boil. Lower heat to maintain a gentle simmer.

While the broth heats, combine beef, Shaoxing wine, sesame oil, 1 tablespoon of the cornstarch, 1 teaspoon salt and ¼ teaspoon white pepper in a medium bowl. Mix with chopsticks or a fork until marinade is absorbed and no dry spots remain.
Break the meat mixture up a bit and then add to the pot of broth, stirring to break it up into small pieces. Skim off any foam that rises to the surface.

In a small bowl, combine remaining 3 tablespoons cornstarch with 3 tablespoons cold water and stir until dissolved. Add the cornstarch mixture to the pot and simmer, stirring, until thickened, about 2 minutes. Taste and adjust salt.
Reduce the heat so the broth is no longer simmering and slowly pour in the egg whites in a thin stream to create delicate ribbons, pausing occasionally to gently stir the soup.
Add tofu and mushrooms and return to a simmer for a minute or two. Just before serving, stir in cilantro and cook until bright green and wilted, about 1 minute.
Serve sprinkled with more cilantro and white pepper.
